New Zealand Student Visa Process

Official step-by-step roadmap from university offer to visa stamp

1

Apply & Receive Offer of Place

Obtain formal Offer of Place from an approved New Zealand education provider.

2

Prepare Financial Evidence & Medical

Demonstrate $20,000 NZD living costs + tuition fee funds.

3

Submit Online Visa (Approval in Principle)

Submit application on Immigration Online to receive Approval in Principle (AIP).

4

Pay Tuition Fee After AIP

Pay full 1st-year tuition fee only after receiving formal AIP from INZ.

5

Receive E-Visa

Receive official Fee Paying Student E-Visa to travel to New Zealand.

Frequently Asked Questions

Country-specific answers verified by ALO Education compliance

What is Approval in Principle (AIP) in New Zealand visa?

AIP means Immigration New Zealand has approved your visa in principle; you only pay tuition fees to the university after AIP is granted.

How long is the Post-Study Work Visa in New Zealand?

Graduates of Master's (Level 9) and PhD (Level 10) programs receive a 3-year open Post-Study Work Visa.

How much bank balance is required for New Zealand Student Visa?

You must demonstrate 1 year of tuition fees + $20,000 NZD living expenses held for at least 6 months with verified financial source documents.

What is the special tuition benefit for international PhD students in NZ?

International PhD students pay the same low domestic tuition fees as local Kiwi citizens (approximately $7,000 - $9,000 NZD per year).

Are all 8 universities in New Zealand government-funded?

Yes, all 8 universities in New Zealand are state-funded public institutions ranked among the top 3% in the world.

Can international students work part-time in New Zealand?

Yes, students on a Fee Paying Student Visa can work up to 20 hours per week during term time and 40 hours per week during scheduled holidays.

What is the New Zealand Green List?

The Green List includes in-demand occupations (engineering, IT, healthcare, teaching) that offer fast-track pathways to residence.

What is Te Pūkenga in New Zealand?

Te Pūkenga is New Zealand's national institute of skills and technology, uniting 16 regional polytechnics across the country.

Can my partner work while I study in New Zealand?

Partners of students studying Level 9 Master's or Level 10 PhD programs can apply for an open partner work visa.

What English tests are accepted by Immigration New Zealand?

IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced, and OET.

What is the minimum IELTS required for New Zealand Master's?

Typically 6.5 overall with no individual band below 6.0.

When are the main intakes in New Zealand?

Semester 1 starts in February/March, and Semester 2 starts in July.

Is health insurance required in New Zealand?

Yes, all international students must hold comprehensive medical and travel insurance for the full duration of their stay.

Can polytechnic diploma graduates from Bangladesh apply to NZ?

Yes, BTEB diploma graduates can apply for Bachelor's degree pathways or Graduate Diplomas.

What is the minimum hourly wage in New Zealand?

The New Zealand adult minimum wage is $23.15 NZD per hour.

How long does New Zealand student visa processing take?

Standard processing takes 4 to 8 weeks on the Immigration New Zealand online system.

Can parents sponsor my education in New Zealand?

Yes, parents, immediate family members, or official education loans from approved banks in Bangladesh are accepted sponsors.

Where is the biometrics collection done for New Zealand?

At the VFS Global Visa Application Centre in Delta Life Tower, Gulshan-2, Dhaka.

Are scholarships available for Bangladeshi students in NZ?

Yes, universities offer automatic international excellence scholarships of $5,000 to $10,000 NZD for qualified applicants.

How does ALO Education assist with New Zealand applications?

ALO Education guides you through university applications, AIP visa filing, tuition remittance, and pre-departure briefings.
